subject: Reserved headroom & min/max policy for renewal
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@cloudfin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved headroom & min/max policy for renewal

Sara —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Per our renewal discussion, I’m sending a concise proposal for the Dedicated renewal that covers: a modest uplift in reserved GPUs, a small reserved headroom buffer for peak-day activity, and explicit min/max replica settings plus warm-pool sizing so you don’t see cold-start latency during campaign spikes.

High-level ask from CloudFin: 40% expected peak increase during fiscal Q4 campaigns. Our proposal to preserve latency SLOs and predictable unit cost:
- Reserved capacity: increase from 24 -> 32 GPUs (pinned pool)
- Reserved headroom: 10% of peak (pre-allocated burst buffer)
- Autoscale min/max: min 2 replicas, max 10 replicas for the dedicated pool serving CloudFin traffic
- Warm pool: maintain 2 warm replicas (pre-initialized model contexts) to reduce scale-up lag to ~3s median
- Scale-up lag guardrail: prioritize warm-pool step-up, fall back to cross-region warm pool if cold start exceeds 8s

I’ve attached a short draft of the autoscale policy and sizing spreadsheet for your procurement and engineering teams. Key asks for CloudFin: confirmation on the headroom percentage (we used 10% as a starting point), approval for the 32 GPU reservation, and whether there are any procurement windows we should align with.

Next steps: if you’re comfortable, I’ll circulate a concise contract amendment and loop legal/finance. Karthik — can you review the scale-up latencies in the draft and call out any model-specific caveats? Marissa — can you prepare the price uplift and term language for a 12-month renewal?

Thanks —
Rishi
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Reserved headroom & min/max policy for renewal

Rishi —

Appreciate the summary and the docs. A few quick notes from our side:
- The 40% peak estimate is correct for Black Friday-style bursts; we cannot tolerate >20% latency regressions for user-facing flows.
- The 32 GPU reservation sounds reasonable if the warm pool prevents cold spikes.
- Procurement: our fiscal Q4 begins 2028-10-01; we need the contract signed before 2028-09-15 for budget approval.

Questions:
1) Can you quantify expected per-token cost delta with the 10% headroom (rough monthly run-rate estimate)?
2) If we cap max at 10 replicas, what is our throughput headroom relative to projected peak RPS?

I’ll loop in engineering if we need more detail. Procurement is inclined to the 12-month term.

—Sara
Sr. PM, CloudFin Payments

Sara —

Quick answers:
- Rough monthly run-rate impact: the 10% reserved headroom increases committed capacity and amortized cost by ~12% on top of your baseline committed spend. I’ve asked Marissa to include a detailed line item in the amendment with a scenario table (low/expected/peak).
- Throughput headroom at max=10 replicas: with your current model (gpt-small-ish topology we provisioned), 10 replicas gives ~3.6x baseline throughput vs. min=2. That maps to ~1.8x projected peak RPS in our conservative forecast; the warm pool and headroom handle burst smoothing.

Karthik will add notes on scale-up timing and model-context warm initialization. We recommend a 2-warm replica minimum for user-facing routes, can raise to 3 if CloudFin wants sub-2s tail latency during the heaviest traffic.

If procurement needs an amortized monthly number now I can push a quick breakdown this afternoon.

Cheers —
Rishi

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, CloudFin Procurement <procurement@cloudfin.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved headroom & min/max policy for renewal

Sara / team —

I reviewed the draft autoscale policy in rdw-dedicated-autoscale-draft.pdf and the sizing spreadsheet. A few technical clarifications and recommendations:

1) Scale-up lag: our measurements (same model family) show median cold-start CPU+GPU init at ~6.5s; with a 2-rep warm pool we observe median warm-step-up to be ~2.8s. The recommended guardrail is: warm_pool >= 2 for primary user-facing routes; if you require <2s tail we should set warm_pool=3.

2) Min/Max mapping: min=2 ensures cost-floor and immediate availability for light traffic; max=10 is conservative for a 32 GPU reservation assuming replica-sizing of 3 GPUs per replica (we suggested 32 GPUs so you have a little headroom for larger replica sizes). If CloudFin wants a tighter cost cap, we can lower max to 8 and compensate by increasing headroom to 15% for burst smoothing.

3) Cross-region fallback: we can enable cross-region warm-pools (secondary region) as an emergency fallthrough to keep latency within SLOs if your primary region experiences saturation. This would be billed as on-demand usage and only invoked on sustained scale events.

I’m attaching a short technical appendix and a small change to the policy wording to make the warm-pool behavior deterministic in step-ups.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: rdw-dedicated-autoscale-draft.pdf)

Rishi / Karthik —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. Procurement reviewed the numbers and CloudFin is comfortable proceeding with:
- 32 GPU reserved pool for 12 months (starts 2028-10-01)
- Reserved headroom 12% (we nudged from 10% after seeing Marissa’s draft pricing)
- Autoscale min/max: min=2 / max=9 (we agreed to slightly tighter max to control monthly variance)
- Warm pool: 2 replicas for user-facing routes; enable cross-region warm fallback as an opt-in (we’ll request it only if we see issues after go-live)

Sara
Sr. PM, CloudFin Payments
